title: Left-shift deployment scratchpad: early-safety canary hypotheses and telemetry checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for experimenting with a "left-shift" approach to release safety: push early, small-scope verification further left (pre-prod / staging shadow) and only then open client-facing traffic. Goal: catch behavioral regressions earlier, reduce blast radius, and shorten time-to-confidence for model flips and runtime changes.

Quick summary/idea:
- Run a tiny, instrumented cohort through the new model/runtime revision but start inside an internal sandbox that mimics warm KV/cache state and hot-client patterns (not full prod traffic).
- Use a combination of deterministic test prompts + a live-sampled subset of requests (1 in 10k) mirrored to staging-shadow (no impact) so we can assert semantics + latency cost.
- Promote to a micro-cohort (0.1–0.5% traffic) only after the staged telemetry looks stable for X windows.

Hypotheses to validate (explicit):
1) Early prefix-cache divergence will surface within first 30k tokens of mirrored load — we should be able to detect 95th pct mismatch in KV-hits within 6 hours.
2) Small changes in kernel selection cause small tail-latency regressions, not QPS-wide; 95th latency is the most informative signal.
3) Model output quality regressions show up in a specific subset of Eval prompts (few-shot hallucination seens) before general-purpose metrics move.

Micro-canary plan (iterative steps):
- Stage 0: local + CI smoke (no live requests). Confirm unit tests, perf harness.
- Stage 1: staging-shadow (mirroring only, sampling 1:10000). Collect: latencies, token-cost, top-k logprobs, response-length distribution, key model features (safety labels if available). Duration: 24–72h.
- Stage 2: internal micro-cohort (dev orgs + internal beta users) at 0.05% traffic. Enable a lightweight circuit-breaker on client errors. Duration: rolling 72h with daily review.
- Stage 3: slow ramp to 0.5% with affinity to non-critical client cohorts.
- Stage 4: normal rollout if no red flags.

Observability checklist (signals to watch closely):
- infra: 95th and 99th CPU/GPU utilization per node, kernel queue length spikes.
- latency: server_p95_token_ms, server_p99_token_ms, cold-start tail events, KV cache miss ratio (per-tenant).
- errors: 5xx rate per-route, model-failed-inference counts, decoding timeouts.
- quality: rerank delta on evaluation seed set, hallucination-rate proxy (low confidence + contradictory fact patterns), stop-token anomalies.
- cost: tokens-per-request distribution, average tokens per session, billing-estimated uplift percent.
- stability: memory growth / leaks in runtime over windowed 6h periods.
- user signals: client-side retries, SDK error count, feature-flag-enforced fallback hits.

Alert thresholds (initial proposals — conservative):
- p99 latency +30% over baseline for > 20 minutes -> automatic traffic hold (pin back).
- sustained p95 latency +20% for 1 hour -> page on-call.
- error rate > 0.5% absolute lift over baseline for 30m -> page + hold.
- rerank delta > 5% on seed prompts for 1 evaluation run -> review, possible block.

Traffic steering and guardrails:
- route all micro-cohort traffic via a dedicated pathway with easy pin-back switch (feature flag + route override).
- maintain fallback model variant (older quantized model) with compatibility checks; automatic fallback if memory OOMs or decode errors spike.
- add weighted-sampling policy that favors non-safety-critical tenants first.

Rollback decision matrix (quick idea):
- severity high (user-facing correctness regression, safety): immediate rollback to last healthy model and page SRE+ML lead.
- severity medium (latency/cost): pause ramp, rollback if no improvement in 30–60m.
- severity low (minor metric drift): continue ramp with close monitoring and AB test.

Preflight checklist (pre-stage1):
- confirm telemetry keys wired into dash (p95/p99, KV-miss, token-cost).
- smoke run with synthetic seed set that includes known edge prompts.
- verify rollback artifact exists and route override tested (simulate toggle).
- ensure on-call calendar has coverage for first 72h + one follow-up deep-dive slot.
- note: get approval from product/stability owner for cohort selection.

Post-deploy observations (notes format):
- keep a running log of anomalies in the first 6h, 24h, 72h. Save examples (request, response, model-version, kernel-version, node-id).
- tag incidents with small labels: "latency-spike", "hallucination-sample", "kv-diverge".
- capture one clean example of success (stable latency + matching eval pass).

Open questions / TODOs (my personal action list):
- [ ] Lina: add 10 seed prompts that historically catch hallucination regressions. (Lina)
- [ ] Marcus: create a dashboard tile that overlays p95 latency vs KV-miss ratio by model-version. (Marcus)
- [ ] Me (Nora): write quick script to pull 10k mirrored requests and diff top-5 tokens per position (tooling).
- [ ] Priya: propose cohort list (non-critical customers) and confirm legal/data considerations. (Priya)
- [ ] Decide on hold-duration policy: 30m vs 1h for automatic pinback.

Final thoughts (scratchpad):
- want the left-shift to reduce time-to-confidence, but the instrumentation burden is real. Keep initial plan narrow: one model flip + one kernel change at a time.
- prioritize signals that are actionable: latency spikes and clear correctness failures. Avoid overfitting to noise (small rerank delta alone shouldn't stop a roll).
- remember: the easiest way to reduce blast radius is tighter cohort fences + automatic route pin.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc intentionally messy. When something works, migrate cleaned steps into the team playbook and link INF ticket.
